blocks.text: HULDAH THE PROPHETESS, IN JOSIAH'S JERUSALEM · TWO KINGDOMS
Huldah. Asked about the book found in the temple, she answered for the LORD: evil on “this place”, peace for the king.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophetess
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Josiah
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
The king's men “went unto Huldah the prophetess … and they communed with her”.
THE CALL
How the word came
The king's men “went unto Huldah the prophetess … and they communed with her”. 2 Kings 22:14
She answered in the LORD's name: “Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Tell the man that sent you to me”. 2 Kings 22:15 2 Chronicles 34:23
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Josiah
KING OF JUDAH
Josiah
“Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the LORD”
2 Kings 22:19 (KJV) →
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
Evil upon this place
“therefore my wrath shall be kindled against this place, and shall not be quenched.”
2 Kings 22:17 (KJV) →
Because thine heart was tender
“thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace; and thine eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place.”
2 Kings 22:20 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO THE KING'S MESSENGERS
“Tell the man that sent you to me”
2 Kings 22:15 (KJV) →
TO JOSIAH, THROUGH HIS MESSENGERS
“Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the LORD”
2 Kings 22:19 (KJV) →
Jerusalem · She “dwelt in Jerusalem in the college”; what that means is a question below
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with her, and against her
Shallum, her husband
Hilkiah the priest
Ahikam son of Shaphan
Shaphan the scribe
Achbor son of Michaiah
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture tells nothing more of Huldah after her answer to the king. 2 Kings 22:20
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
A school or house of instruction
The Targum, as reported by Ellicott and Gill; Geneva notes (1599); Matthew Poole (1683–1685)

The Geneva note: “Or the house of doctrine, which was near the temple”. Poole: “where the sons of the prophets, or others who devoted themselves to the study of God's word, used to meet”. 2 Kings 22:14 [24][83][36]
A district of the city, “the second quarter”
Ellicott's commentary; J. R. Lumby (1887); C. F. Keil (1872); the Pulpit Commentary

The Hebrew mishneh means “second”, as in “an howling from the second” (Zephaniah 1:10) and “second over the city” (Nehemiah 11:9). Ellicott: “The word really means the second part of the city”; the Revised Version reads “in the second quarter” (Lumby). 2 Kings 22:14 Zephaniah 1:10 Nehemiah 11:9 [16][74][67][95]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
2 Kings 22 2 Kings 23 2 Chronicles 34
PASSAGES · 3
2 Kings 22:8–20 2 Kings 23:1–3 2 Chronicles 34:14–28
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture names Huldah only in this one event, told in Kings and in Chronicles.
It does not say why she, rather than another prophet, was consulted.

Kings and Chronicles do not themselves say that her word came to pass; they tell Josiah's covenant, his death at Megiddo and, later, the fall of Jerusalem. 2 Kings 24:2 sends the bands against Judah “according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by his servants the prophets”, without naming her.
